summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, chronic venous stasis ulcers, lipodermatosclerosis, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for worsening cellulitis around a left lower extremity ulcer. She presented with spreading erythema, pain, and drainage but no fever. IV vancomycin was initiated and continued throughout the hospitalization. A PICC line was placed to complete antibiotic therapy at home. Dermatology recommended discontinuing silver chloride on the ulcer due to potential irritation and advised diluted vinegar soaks followed by mupirocin and proper dressings. Imaging ruled out DVT, and asymptomatic bacteriuria was not treated. Her infection improved clinically, and she was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics and wound care, with follow-up planned with dermatology.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Ulcer of other part of lower limb
